body.statement:
Fix a deterministic sequence of supplied pairs \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\), and set \(N=3n\).  Suppose that
\[
 \varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 =o\!\left((\log(3n))^{-1/2}\right)
\]
along the indices for which \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\).  Assume the following conditional-transfer compatibility condition.  There are constants \(A=A(C_{\mathrm{env}},c_\xi)>0\), \(K=K(C_{\mathrm{env}},c_\xi)\ge e(1\vee C_{\mathrm{env}})\), and \(h_0=h_0(C_{\mathrm{env}},c_\xi)>0\), independent of \(n\), with \(A^2\ge c_\xi\), such that:

\(\mathrm{CT1}\) for every sufficiently large \(n\), there are a covariate law \(P_{X,n}\) and measurable functions \(g_{*,n},q_{*,n}\) for which, for every \(|v|\le h_0\), the law \(P_{n,v}\) defined by
\[
 X\sim P_{X,n},\qquad
 T=g_{*,n}(X)+\eta,\qquad
 Y=q_{*,n}(X)+v\eta+A\zeta,
 \qquad \eta,\zeta\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1),
\]
with \((\eta,\zeta)\perp X\), belongs to \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and satisfies \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P_{n,v})\);

\(\mathrm{CT2}\) whenever \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\), the fixed source center \((\widehat g,\widehat q/A)\) and radii
\[
 a_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}}{K},
 \qquad
 b_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{q,n}}{KA}
\]
satisfy the hypotheses of \(\textup{lem:jms-support-localized-product-benchmark}\), and the measurable outcome-rescaling map \(S_A(x,t,y)=(x,t,Ay)\) sends every law \(R\) in the two cited fuzzy supports to \(P=R\circ S_A^{-1}\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) with \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\) and \(\theta_0(P)=A\vartheta(R)\).

Then there exists \(c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(c_\xi\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every interval \(C_n\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
also satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|\ge c d_n^- ,
\]
and therefore \(L_G(C_n)\ge c d_n^-\).  The conditional variance restriction defining \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\), as well as \((\mathrm{CT1})\)--\((\mathrm{CT2})\), is confined to this Gaussian lower-bound subexperiment and is not a hypothesis of the adaptive upper-frontier theorem.
body.justification: The theorem records the source-supported Gaussian coordinate on transfer-compatible supplied-fit sequences, with the fuzzy nuisance-product/log and parametric two-point mechanisms proved separately.
body.gap: The result remains conditional on exact support compatibility and retains \(\Lambda_n\); the frozen core does not prove either unconditional transfer for every supplied fit or the full \(d_n\) coordinate.
body.consumer: On its stated subexperiment it rules out Gaussian-coordinate expected length below \(d_n^-\), without asserting a global union-supremum improvement or a matching vector frontier.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(N=3n\).  By \(\textup{def:projected-experiment}\), concatenating \(D_K,D_D,D_A\) identifies \(Q_P\) with \(P^{\otimes N}\).  Hence an interval measurable in the three evaluation folds is an interval in the \(N\)-observation experiment.

We first prove the nuisance-product lower bound on every positive-product index.  Put
\[
 a_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}}{K},
 \qquad
 b_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{q,n}}{KA}.
\]
Because \(A\) and \(K\) are fixed positive constants, the assumed product condition gives
\[
 a_Nb_N
 =\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K^2A}
 =o\!\left((\log N)^{-1/2}\right).
\]
Condition \((\mathrm{CT2})\) permits the invocation of \(\textup{lem:jms-support-localized-product-benchmark}\) with supplied source fit \((\widehat g,\widehat q/A)\), source radii \((a_N,b_N)\), and \(s=8\).  This is an assumed conditional transfer of the cited support; it is not inferred from a lower bound over an unspecified larger source class.

The source's recentering step moves a bounded center inward by at most half of each nuisance radius and uses a half-radius construction around the recentered pair; the triangle inequality then keeps that entire construction in the original radius ball.  Consequently, \((\mathrm{CT2})\) does not require \(\|\widehat g\|_\infty\) or \(\|\widehat q\|_\infty\) to be a small multiple of \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), nor does it separately require \(\varepsilon_{g,n}+\varepsilon_{q,n}\to0\).  Some compatibility premise nevertheless cannot be removed from this proof: \(\textup{def:supplied-fit-set}\) gives only \(L^8(P_X)\) control, which neither supplies the pointwise bounded center required by construction (44) nor guarantees that the displayed supremum contains any law for an arbitrary external fit pair.  Condition \((\mathrm{CT2})\) states exactly the support inclusion used below.

To track the outcome rescaling, let \(\widehat\theta\) be an arbitrary estimator in the transformed experiment and define the source-scale estimator
\[
 \widehat\vartheta_R(z_1,\ldots,z_N)
 =A^{-1}\widehat\theta\bigl(S_Az_1,\ldots,S_Az_N\bigr).
\]
Take \(\gamma=3/4\), which is larger than \(\alpha\) because \(\alpha<1/2\).  The cited lemma supplies an \(R\) in one of its two fuzzy supports such that
\[
 R^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
 |\widehat\vartheta_R-\vartheta(R)|
 \ge c_\gamma a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \right\}\ge\gamma .
\]
Let \(P=R\circ S_A^{-1}\).  By \((\mathrm{CT2})\), \(P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\), the supplied pair is in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\), and \(\theta_0(P)=A\vartheta(R)\).  Since \(S_A\) is a measurable bijection, the preceding display is exactly
\[
 Q_P\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta-\theta_0(P)|
 \ge c_\gamma A a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \right\}\ge\gamma .
\]
Notice that the source outcome radius used here is \(b_N=\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\), so the source separation is multiplied by \(A\) only after the pushforward.  In particular,
\[
 A a_Nb_N
 =\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K^2}.
\]

Let \(\ell_n=1\vee\log(1/\varepsilon_{g,n})\).  Since \(0<\varepsilon_{g,n}\le C_{\mathrm{env}}\) on a positive-product index and \(K\ge e(1\vee C_{\mathrm{env}})\),
\[
 \log(1/a_N)=\log(K/\varepsilon_{g,n})\ge\ell_n.
\]
Moreover, \(\log(3n)\le c_0\log(en)\) for a universal \(c_0\).  It follows from \(\textup{def:rate-scales}\) that
\[
 A a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \ge c_1\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 \min\!\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{\ell_n}{\log(en)}\right)^3\right\}
 =c_1\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n,
\]
where \(c_1>0\) depends only on \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\) and \(c_\xi\) through \(A\) and \(K\).  Thus every estimator has, on a law in the transferred fuzzy support, error at least \(c_2\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\) with probability at least \(\gamma\).

Every transferred support law lies in \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal G_n\subseteq\mathcal U_n\), and its supplied pair lies in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\), by \((\mathrm{CT2})\), \(\textup{def:gaussian-nondegenerate-subclass}\), and \(\textup{def:honesty-union}\).  Union honesty therefore implies honesty over this support.  Applying \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) with \(r=c_2\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\), \(\beta=\gamma\), and the class equal to the transferred fuzzy support yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c_3\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n.
\]
When \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}=0\), this display remains true because its right-hand side is zero, and no fuzzy-support transfer is invoked.

We next prove the parametric lower bound by a distinct two-point construction.  Fix
\[
 \beta=\frac{\alpha+1/2}{2},
 \qquad \alpha<\beta<1/2.
\]
Use the covariate law and anchor regressions in \((\mathrm{CT1})\).  For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), set \(v_0=0\), \(v_1=\Delta=hN^{-1/2}\), and let \(P_j=P_{n,v_j}\), where \(h>0\) will be fixed below.  Taking \(h\le h_0\) ensures \(|v_j|\le h_0\).  The equations in \((\mathrm{CT1})\) give
\[
 Y=v_jT+\{q_{*,n}(X)-v_jg_{*,n}(X)\}+A\zeta.
\]
Thus \(\theta_0(P_j)=v_j\), \(f_{0,j}=q_{*,n}-v_jg_{*,n}\), and \(\xi_j=A\zeta\).  In particular,
\[
 E_{P_j}[\xi_j\mid X,T]=0,
 \qquad
 E_{P_j}[\xi_j^2\mid X,T]=A^2\ge c_\xi.
\]
Condition \((\mathrm{CT1})\) supplies the remaining envelope, Gaussian-branch, and supplied-fit membership conditions, so \(P_j\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P_j)\).

Under \(P_0\), conditional division of the two Gaussian outcome densities gives the one-observation likelihood ratio
\[
 L=\frac{dP_1}{dP_0}
 =\exp\!\left\{
 \frac{\Delta\eta\{Y-q_{*,n}(X)\}}{A^2}
 -\frac{\Delta^2\eta^2}{2A^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Under \(P_0\), \(\{Y-q_{*,n}(X)\}/A=\zeta\) is standard Gaussian and independent of \(\eta\).  Its moment-generating function gives
\[
 E_{P_0}[L^2\mid X,\eta]
 =\exp(\Delta^2\eta^2/A^2).
\]
Since \(\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), direct Gaussian integration yields
\[
 E_{P_0}[L^2]
 =\left(1-\frac{2\Delta^2}{A^2}\right)^{-1/2}.
\]
Independence of the \(N\) observations consequently gives
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N}\right)
 =\left(1-\frac{2h^2}{A^2N}\right)^{-N/2}-1.
\]
If \(2h^2/A^2\le1/2\), then \(-\log(1-x)\le2x\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\) implies
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N}\right)
 \le \exp(2h^2/A^2)-1.
\]
Choose \(h>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(A\), and \(h_0\), small enough that the last expression is at most \(4(1-2\beta)^2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz then gives
\[
 \left\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12E_{P_0^{\otimes N}}|L_N-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N})}
 \le1-2\beta.
\]

For an arbitrary estimator \(\widehat\theta\), the events
\[
 A_j=\{|\widehat\theta-v_j|<\Delta/2\},\qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
are disjoint.  Therefore
\[
 P_0^{\otimes N}(A_0)+P_1^{\otimes N}(A_1)
 \le P_0^{\otimes N}(A_0)+P_0^{\otimes N}(A_1)
 +\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le1+\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}},
\]
and hence
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}
 P_j^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta-v_j|\ge\frac{h}{2\sqrt N}
 \right\}
 \ge\frac{1-\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{2}
 \ge\beta.
\]
The two laws are in the honesty union and are compatible with the supplied fits by \((\mathrm{CT1})\).  A second application of \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\), now with the class \(\{P_0,P_1\}\), yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|\ge c_4N^{-1/2}\ge c_5n^{-1/2}.
\]

The same supremum is bounded below by both the parametric and nuisance-product terms.  Therefore \(\max\{x,y\}\ge(x+y)/2\) and \(\textup{def:rate-scales}\) give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c\left\{n^{-1/2}+
 \varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\right\}
 =c d_n^-.
\]
Finally, \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal G_n\) and \(\textup{def:length-vector}\) imply \(L_G(C_n)\ge c d_n^-\).  The proof used the conditional outcome-variance restriction and the two transfer conditions only for these lower-bound subexperiments.
